findings.reason: the section's new queued arm is anchored on a symbol a worker cannot open, and a wrong anchor sends it to re-derive which record the queued pointer is built from instead of editing the named site.
findings.text: the deliverable names `_queued_dispatch_record` as the writer of `launcher_host: None`, but no such symbol exists in the repository; the function at the cited line is `_queued_request_record` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:213, key at :249), so a worker grepping the named symbol finds nothing and cannot tell whether the line reference or the name is the stale half

findings.reason: a worker can read the second clause as describing current behaviour and make no change at that merge, in which case the added queued-launch arm fails and the node's single fix site is never modified.
findings.text: the deliverable says `attach_launch_identity` "publishes no host, so the None survives the launch; that merge also sets the launching host", which asserts both that the merge publishes no host (true today: the record built at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2994 carries no `launcher_host`, so `{**pointer, **record}` keeps the queued None) and that it sets the launching host (false today), leaving the one site the queued done-when depends on as an unresolved either/or

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the queued write site is named `_queued_dispatch_record`, a symbol that exists nowhere in the repository; the function whose line 249 carries `launcher_host: None` is `_queued_request_record` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:213).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — both new arms are falsifiable: the resume arm fails at base (pointer keeps A and the second resume is refused) and the new queued-launch arm fails at base too, because `_queued_request_record` writes `launcher_host: None` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:249) and `_launched_on_this_host` treats a None host as unattributed (reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:1226), so the pointer can never read B without the fix.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gate logs are required under the run directory, opening with the revision and literal command and ending in `EXIT=`, and the new test sits in `tests/`, so nothing lands on a scratch or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test and the section name the mechanism (`test_a_resume_records_the_host_that_launched_it.py`, `attach_launch_identity`, `_stamp_pointer_launch_host`) with no plan label, stage name, ticket number or changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the sentence that carries the new queued mechanism contradicts itself: it says `attach_launch_identity` "publishes no host, so the None survives the launch", then states that same merge "also sets the launching host".
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the section has one goal, that each launch attempt records its own launching host; the queued path is a second write site for that one fact, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` now carries `s50: ["a-dispatch-returns-without-its-worker#s25"]` (plan.html:22), that plan's §25 exists at a-dispatch-returns-without-its-worker.html:1051 and its write paths include `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`, which §50 also writes, so the declared wait is both present and correct.
